chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged that the slander (fabrication of accusation) is three, meaning three aspects: when a man accuses a man of adultery, and when he says 'his mother is an adulteress', and when he is called by the name of someone other than his father; for that there is a Hadd (fixed penalty) of eighty (lashes).
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He said regarding the man when he slanders a married woman: He is lashed eighty (lashes), whether he is free or a slave.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of slander (Qadhf) that incur a penalty of eighty lashes according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the specific legal categories of Qadhf (slander) as adjudicated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), tracing the precedent back to Imam Ali (AS). It clarifies that the fixed penalty of eighty lashes applies uniformly to free and enslaved accusers, emphasizing the jurisprudential consistency in punishing false accusations of adultery against the 'Muhsan' (chaste/married) individual.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrhim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws judged that the fabrications are three, meaning three aspects of it – when the man accuses the man with the adultery, and when he says that his mother is an adulteress, and when he claims that he is for other than his father. So that, regarding it is a Penalty (Hadd) of eighty (lashes)’.[675]
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama’at,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said regarding the man when he slanders the married woman. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘He would be whipped eighty lashes, whether he is free or a slave’.
